content.user_title: Discover and Prioritize Data Use Scenarios
content.value_statement: Organizations often overlook valuable uses for data they already hold. This skill scans industries, ranks opportunities, and defines evidence needed for validation.
actual_capabilities: Scans ISIC industry categories for potential uses of an available dataset.
Applies analogy, value-chain, pain-point, and data-combination discovery methods.
Maps industry problems to relevant data requirements and possible buyers.
Ranks scenarios by value and feasibility in a four-quadrant matrix.
Defines validation evidence covering buyer demand, payment intent, and deliverables.
Performs an initial check of whether existing authorization covers a proposed use.
limitations: It does not replace legal, regulatory, accounting, or licensed professional advice.
It cannot prove buyer demand without interviews, budgets, contracts, or comparable paid cases.
Its opportunity rankings depend on complete and accurate descriptions of available data.
It provides initial compliance screening, not a final authorization or privacy determination.

use_cases.title: Expand an enterprise data portfolio
use_cases.description: Identify credible internal and external uses for existing operational, customer, or sensor data.

use_cases.title: Select data products for validation
use_cases.description: Rank candidate scenarios and choose up to three opportunities for focused market testing.

use_cases.title: Explore cross-industry demand
use_cases.description: Map a dataset to unfamiliar industries while recording likely buyers, value, feasibility, and authorization concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Generate an initial scenario list
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this data inventory: [inventory]. Suggest practical use scenarios, likely users, required data fields, and assumptions that need validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery from a clear data inventory

prompt_templates.title: Scan industries with ISIC
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan these datasets across relevant ISIC sectors: [datasets]. For each opportunity, explain the problem, buyer, data contribution, and expected deliverable.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize candidate scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these scenarios: [scenarios]. Score value and feasibility using stated evidence, place each in a quadrant, and recommend three validation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Design a validation and compliance plan
prompt_templates.prompt: For these priority scenarios: [scenarios], define buyer interviews, payment evidence, deliverable tests, data gaps, authorization checks, decision gates, and a ninety-day plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation planning for selected opportunities

output_examples.input: We have regional weather, irrigation, and crop yield data. Find valuable scenarios beyond internal reporting.
output: Priority scenario: farm irrigation recommendations for agricultural cooperatives.
Buyer evidence needed: named cooperative users, seasonal budget, and an agreed recommendation report.
Feasibility checks: field coverage, update frequency, farm identifiers, and permission for advisory use.

output_examples.input: Rank demand forecasting, insurance risk scoring, and academic research access for our mobility data.
output: Prioritize demand forecasting when buyer access and aggregated data are already available.
Treat insurance scoring as a high-risk scenario until authorization, fairness, and regulated-use requirements are resolved.
Keep research access as a reserve scenario with de-identification and institutional review conditions.

output_examples.input: Create a validation plan for an energy benchmarking data product.
output_examples.output: Interview five facility managers, confirm two budget owners, test a sample benchmark report, verify usage rights, and stop if no paid pilot emerges.

best_practices: Provide a precise data inventory including fields, time range, quality, granularity, ownership, authorization, and current uses.
Require sources for comparable cases and label every unsupported statement as an assumption.
Validate no more than three priority scenarios and include one option testable within ninety days.
anti_patterns: Do not equate a long scenario list with verified market demand.
Do not assign revenue estimates without a stated basis, buyer evidence, and uncertainty range.
Do not reuse data across industries before checking consent, contracts, privacy, and sector rules.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide data fields, coverage, format, quality, update frequency, ownership, authorization, current uses, and known restrictions.

faq.question: Does the skill cover every industry?
faq.answer: It can scan major ISIC sectors, but the useful depth depends on available evidence and domain context.

faq.question: How does it decide which scenarios are priorities?
faq.answer: It compares buyer value with feasibility, including data readiness, compliance, technical delivery, and buyer access.

faq.question: Can it confirm that buyers will pay?
faq.answer: No. Payment intent requires direct evidence such as interviews, budgets, paid pilots, contracts, or comparable transactions.

faq.question: Does it provide legal compliance approval?
faq.answer: No. It flags authorization and cross-industry concerns for review by qualified legal, privacy, or regulatory professionals.

faq.question: What deliverables can it prepare?
faq.answer: It can prepare scenario inventories, industry scans, pain-point mappings, priority matrices, validation plans, and scenario briefs.
